function: Downlink CSI compression, quantization and reconstruction for FDD massive MIMO: encoder at the UE, VQ-VAE quantizer (VQCFB), decoder at the BS (pp. 2-3).
system: Single-cell OFDM FDD massive MIMO: Nt=32 BS antennas, one UE antenna, Nc=1024 subcarriers; indoor 5.3 GHz and outdoor 300 MHz; no RIS (pp. 2-3).
method: CsiConformer (four Conformer blocks per encoder and decoder, self-attention plus convolution) with VQCFB vector quantizer; end-to-end training on MSE plus quantization loss, implicitly supervised (pp. 2-3).
data_channel: COST 2100 default settings: indoor picocellular 5.3 GHz and outdoor rural 300 MHz; 150,000 simulated CSI split 100,000 training, 30,000 validation, 20,000 testing (pp. 3-4).
test_conditions: Random non-overlapping split of the simulated CSI into train, validation and test; indoor and outdoor, CR 4-64, 3-5 quantization bits; scenario variations left as future work (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Learned CSI networks: CsiNet+, CRNet, CLNet, TransNet, DCRNet; quantizers: uniform and mu-law (traditional), Base VQ (VQ-VAE), entropy coding; no compressive-sensing baseline (pp. 4-5).
metrics: NMSE (dB) versus compression ratio and quantization bits; FLOPs; feedback overhead r in bits per channel element (pp. 4-5).
complexity: FLOPs in Table I (CsiConformer 22.86M at CR 4 to 20.89M at CR 64; 37.36% fewer than TransNet on average); VQ codebook has 1024 parameters (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 3: "We adopt the default settings in COST2100" (indoor picocellular 5.3 GHz and outdoor rural 300 MHz channels are generated for training and testing).
q2_support: p. 5: "we will conduct additional simulations across the scenario" (future work; every result comes from a random split of the simulated CSI, p. 4, with no training on one scenario and testing on another).
q3_support: p. 5: "Traditional quantization schemes are coarse in" (uniform and mu-law quantizers versus VQCFB on NMSE, Fig. 4); p. 4: "including CsiNet+ [9], CRNet [10], CLNet [11]," (earlier learned networks on NMSE, Table I).
q4_support: p. 4: "CsiConformer requires 37.36% fewer FLOPs on" (Table I lists the FLOPs of every network; the VQ codebook adds 1024 parameters).
q5_support: p. 4: "The total 150,000 simulated CSI are randomly split into" (own data generated with COST 2100 settings; no link to code or data; the only link, footnote 1, is the thop FLOPs library).
notes: Published IEEE Communications Letters version. Table I was read from the page image. q3 rests on the uniform and mu-law quantizers, which the paper calls traditional quantization schemes but trains end-to-end inside the DL pipeline; the compression comparison of Table I has only learned networks and no compressive-sensing baseline, so the reviewer should confirm q3. q5: the COST 2100 setup (Nt=32, Nc=1024, 150,000 samples, 5.3 GHz indoor, 300 MHz outdoor) resembles the widely used CsiNet dataset, but the paper does not say it uses that public dataset and gives no link.
